sources.title: Penny Wong: parliamentary service, ministerial appointments and qualifications
sources.findings: Read parliamentary biography MPID00AOU: birth 5 November 1968, Kota Kinabalu; BA(Juris), LLB(Hons), Graduate Diploma in Legal Practice. First elected 2001 and re-elected 2007/2013/2016/2022; service and committee records from July 2002. Climate and Water from 3 December 2007; energy efficiency added 8 March 2010; Finance and Deregulation 14 September 2010–18 September 2013; Foreign Affairs from 23 May 2022. Government leadership in Senate 26 June–18 September 2013 and from 31 May 2022; opposition leadership 14 October 2013–23 May 2022; shadow foreign affairs 23 July 2016–23 May 2022. Parliamentary leadership is not Senate presidency. Historical profession chronology: industrial officer 1990–1994, NSW adviser 1995–1996, lawyer 1996–1999, legal officer 1999–2002. Current office corroborated by a dated 2026 ministry record rather than solely this biography’s crawl date.

sources.title: Official biography of Senator the Hon Penny Wong
sources.findings: Read foreign minister’s official biography: migration in 1976 at age eight, Adelaide settlement, law/arts study, union and legal work, 2001 election, climate and finance roles, and first woman to lead either government or opposition in the Senate. Finance Minister and Treasurer Wayne Swan are different roles. Developed emissions-trading proposal is not proof that the scheme passed; the separately read 2009 ABC report supplies the failed vote. Government claims about investment, reputation and regional outcomes are not independently audited effects. Search preview of an AAP profile uses 1977 migration; it was not read in full and does not displace the official date.

sources.title: Honorary Doctor of the University citation: degrees, career and Senate entry
sources.findings: Read University of Adelaide honorary Doctor of the University citation: BA majoring in jurisprudence, LLB with honours, undergraduate graduation in 1993, and Graduate Diploma in Legal Practice from the University of South Australia. Honorary doctorate is distinct from a research PhD. The visible PDF gives Saturday 6 May without a year; no ceremony year was inferred from the weekday or search-engine publication timestamp. Some low-quality search previews give 1992 graduation; the profile attributes 1993 to the university citation. It also confirms first election 2001 and taking the seat in July 2002. No personal transcript or certificate inspected.

sources.publisher: Australian Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet
sources.title: Ministerial offices and responsibilities as at 6 November 2026
sources.findings: Read PM&C ministerial offices and responsibilities list dated 6 November 2026: Penny Wong is Cabinet Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs, responsible for the portfolio except trade and tourism. This is a current office record, not a record that she attended every event or held the trade/tourism portfolio. Other ministers’ roles and notices on the page were not assigned to her.

sources.title: Senate rejects emissions-trading legislation, 13 August 2009
sources.findings: Read ABC News report dated 13 August 2009 on Senate rejection of Carbon Pollution Reduction Scheme legislation. Wong said it would be reintroduced; non-government senators opposed the bill. The profile records this August vote only, not a purported final history of every later iteration. Opposition and Greens had differing objections; criticism is not presented as an independent scientific finding. A rejected proposal is not an implemented emissions-trading law.

sources.publisher: Australian Minister for Foreign Affairs and Prime Minister
sources.title: Joint announcement recognising the State of Palestine, 21 September 2025
sources.findings: Read joint prime minister/foreign minister statement of 21 September 2025: Australian recognition of the State of Palestine effective that day, support for a two-state solution, and future consideration of diplomatic relations and embassies as Palestinian Authority reforms progress. Recognition does not prove an embassy opened that day, all reforms were completed, or peace was achieved. This is an Australian government decision, not Wong’s unilateral personal act. Political expectations remain attributed.

sources.title: Defence cooperation and maritime security joint release, 15 November 2026
sources.findings: Read 15 November 2026 joint Albanese/Marles/Wong release: the prime minister witnessed an Australia–Philippines Defence Cooperation Arrangement in Manila; future regional maritime/cyber support includes equipment and training. The release quotes Wong but does not establish her physical presence at that signing. Announced investment and planned capability-building are not fully delivered equipment or independently measured regional security outcomes. No unsupported funding total added.

sources.title: Transcript of interview with Sally Sara, ABC Radio National, 18 November 2026
sources.findings: Read official transcript of Sally Sara’s ABC Radio National interview with Wong on 18 November 2026, including opening and policy discussion. It supports actual current activity and covers West Bank settlement-related sanctions, US–China dialogue/trade and Ukraine. Sanctions rationale and claims about diplomatic results remain government positions; no independent criminal conviction, sanctions-impact audit, aid-donor ranking or verified future leaders’ meeting inferred. The transcript is marked E&OE; original audio and separate legal designation instruments were not reviewed.
